function: Excluded (function): learned STAR network reconstructs human micro-Doppler spectrograms from incomplete 802.11ay CIR estimates for activity recognition, a sensing function outside the seven areas (p. 1, p. 6).
notes: Reason function (code 5), the first code that applies. p. 1: "a neural network that reconstructs micro-Doppler sequences of human movement even from highly incomplete channel measurements"; p. 6: "Our aim is to recover z[t] from the incomplete measurement vector h[t]" to obtain the micro-Doppler spectrum; p. 2: "A classifier is finally used to assess the user activity". The channel is estimated by the standard, not by the model, p. 9: "CIR estimates are obtained in a standard-compliant fashion, using so-called TRN fields of pilot symbols appended as trailers to IEEE 802.11ay packets", so the learned block is not channel estimation (area 2). Codes 1 to 4 do not apply: a research article that proposes and evaluates a method; learned by deep unrolling with trained weights plus attention refinement (p. 7: "and then learnt during training"); signal processing of the CIR, not above the PHY. Borderline with area 5: the link is a monostatic JCS 802.11ay system (p. 5: "CIR estimates are reused (besides using them to decode data) to obtain information about the sensing targets") and p. 14 evaluates the communication overhead that sensing adds, but the learned block sets no beams, waveforms, or resources that serve sensing and communication; it only processes channel estimates for sensing. If the reviewer reads area 5 as covering learned sensing processing in a JCS link, the work needs full grading. The PDF matches its DOI: title and DOI 10.1109/JSTSP.2024.3408041 on p. 1.
